title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: DOREEN ON ICE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Doreen Pickett, a forklift driver in Little Rock, Arkansas.
Her husband Ray asked for one thing: one lap around the ice rink, on their twenty-fifth anniversary.
Doreen had never stood on ice thicker than a snow cone.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: WHOSE SKATES?
segments.quote: The first thing is to love your sport. Never do it to please someone else. It has to be yours.
segments.author: Peggy Fleming
lines: She signed up for lessons with Bud, a retired Zamboni driver.
Bud asked why she came. For Ray, she said. Bud pointed at a poster of Olympic champion Peggy Fleming:
The first thing is to love your sport. Never do it to please someone else. It has to be yours.
So Doreen asked what she wanted. To glide, just once.
She bought her own skates. Purple.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: WOBBLY ANKLES
segments.quote: Build up your weaknesses until they become your strong points.
segments.author: Knute Rockne
lines: Her ankles wobbled like a newborn calf's.
Bud quoted the old Notre Dame coach Knute Rockne:
Build up your weaknesses until they become your strong points.
So at work, waiting for trucks, Doreen stood on one foot.
The guys called her the Flamingo. By December, her ankles were steel.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE HOCKEY BOYS
segments.quote: My courage always rises at every attempt to intimidate me.
segments.author: Jane Austen
lines: One night, college hockey players laughed as she fell. Look out, Grandma's on the ice!
She sat there and remembered her book club's favorite Jane Austen line:
My courage always rises at every attempt to intimidate me.
She got up, skated past them at the speed of a parade float, and waved.
The next week, they held the door for her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE SLUSHY WEEK
segments.quote: Hope is like the sun, which, as we journey toward it, casts the shadow of our burden behind us.
segments.author: Samuel Smiles
lines: Then a warm week turned the ice to slush. She fell six times and nearly quit.
Her mom's old cross-stitch, from the Scottish writer Samuel Smiles, said:
Hope is like the sun, which, as we journey toward it, casts the shadow of our burden behind us.
So Doreen skated at sunrise, facing the light. The falls stopped bothering her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE NIGHT BEFORE
segments.quote: The moment you doubt whether you can fly, you cease for ever to be able to do it.
segments.author: J. M. Barrie
lines: The night before, she couldn't sleep. What if she fell in front of everybody?
Her granddaughter wanted a story by J. M. Barrie, who wrote Peter Pan. One line stopped her:
The moment you doubt whether you can fly, you cease for ever to be able to do it.
So she quit doubting, and slept like a log.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: TWENTY-FIVE YEARS
segments.quote: No man or woman really knows what perfect love is until they have been married a quarter of a century.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: On the big night, Doreen let go of the wall and skated a whole lap by herself.
Ray, who grew up skating in Buffalo, had to chase her. Then he handed her a card from Mark Twain:
No man or woman really knows what perfect love is until they have been married a quarter of a century.
They took a second lap holding hands, bumped, fell, and laughed like newlyweds.

segments.head: GOOD NIGHT
segments.quote: Make it yours. Build up. Stand tall. Face the sun. Don't doubt. Love long.
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: So, make it yours, build up the weak spots, stand tall, face the sun, stop doubting, and love for the long haul.
Me? I tried skating once. The ice won.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
